notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Ezekiel 14 this time. My first attempt to load the source pages was blocked by a tool limit, so no pages were read. That attempt would have opened Enduring Word, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on BibleHub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. My other tools can't reach the internet, so I had no other way to get the commentaries.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything: notes without sources would break those rules.

**What I'd do on the next try:**

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-14/
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/14.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/ezekiel/14.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/ezekiel/14.htm
   - preceptaustin.org (Ezekiel 14 page)
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** the most likely verses are v. 9 ("I the LORD … enticed him") and vv. 4–5 (God answering "according to his idolatry"). For these I'd search ligonier.org, monergism.com, gty.org, desiringgod.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's Notes) and seedbed.com, so each view comes from that tradition's own teachers.
3. **Other views:**
   - The NET Bible notes and bibleodyssey.org on who the "Daniel" of v. 14 is.
   - newadvent.org and catholic.com on vv. 14–20 and what they say about the saints' righteousness and praying on behalf of others.
   - gotquestions.org for any popular modern teaching that cites the chapter.

If you send the request again, I'll start with these pages and write the notes as you laid them out ("v. 4: …"), with a URL after each point.
